source: ADR-0071's re-founding table, 2026-08-11 (#326), superseding the human ruling on #258 as amended by #217 item 9
coverage: This table is not a complete account of what needs routing. Class 6 asserts an invariant no refusal enforces, and its path list names a minority of the gates this project runs; classes 4 and 5 refuse no route at all. A surface this file does not name is uncovered, never cleared. Class ids 1 and 7 are retired by ADR-0071's re-founding table and are never reused, so an id is a stable historical handle rather than a position.

classes.name: orchestration
classes.label: Orchestration
classes.remedy: Keep orchestration on its Claude seat. This is the one provenance rule ADR-0071 ruling 1 left standing, and it is provisional: it says the seat deciding what everything else does should not move before a tested alternative exists, and it ends when the Codex orchestrator backup is built.

classes.name: adr_authorship
classes.label: ADR authorship
classes.remedy: Route ADR authorship to the `planner` seat, whose ordered profile preferences carry it (ADR-0071 ruling 2). It enforces on `docs/adr/`, its own landing surface, rather than on issue phrases alone. The retro half of the class this row descends from is withdrawn by ruling 3 — a retro identifies and files and lands nothing, so it needs no routing rule and its `docs/process-log.md` path went with it.

classes.name: plausible_wrong_fix_goes_green
classes.label: The #181 shape
issue_phrases: plausible wrong fix would also have gone green
plausible wrong fix would also go green
classes.remedy: No mechanical gate distinguishes this diagnosis's plausible wrong fix from the right one, so the remedy is capability rather than provenance: route it to the `planner` seat and escalate. ADR-0071 ruling 5's fourth transferring-escalation condition, `plausible_wrong_fix_goes_green`, fires on exactly this class and names the transfer; the condition and its remedy are data in `config/escalation-conditions.json` and reach an agent as an emission.

classes.name: in_world_landings
classes.label: In-world landings
classes.remedy: A subagent cannot hold the full `just regress` corpus's foreground wait — `.claude/hooks/deny-subagent-waits.py` denies it — so a seat reached as a subagent cannot gate its own in-world work and must not take it. That is the whole of the rule: `just dispatch` launches a top-level session, which the wait hook permits by returning 0 where there is no agent id, so this row refuses no dispatch route. Its two path lists remain the one authority for what an in-world surface is, read by `just land`'s corpus rung, `tools/admission.py` and `tools/brief.py` (#302).

classes.name: gates_themselves
classes.label: Conflict of interest: the gates themselves
classes.remedy: Conflict of interest: no instance authors the gate that judges it. This binds every instance, Claude's included, and is discharged by an independent review under ADR-0071 ruling 4 — which no refusal enforces until step 7's exemption list lands, so today the invariant is asserted and honoured by procedure. It carries no exception, and the withdrawn `Routing-exception: proposal-only` marker went with the framing: an instance that can except itself from the gate that judges it is precisely the shape this class forbids. `.claude/hooks/` and `.claude/settings.json` are here, not dropped: they are the denial layer and the permission allowlist, and the withdrawn gated-semantic-surfaces class was the only routing rule that named them. Coverage is incomplete and this refusal is not evidence otherwise: the list names six tools plus those two paths, and omits `tools/check_adr_form.py`, `tools/check_seat_config.py`, `tools/check_validated_markers.py`, `tools/check_conflict_markers.py`, `tools/check_source_symlink.py`, `tools/export_command_schema.py` and `tools/breaker.py`, along with every gate reached only through `just unit`, `just mutation`, `just land` and `just regress`. A diff touching a gate this list does not name is uncovered, never cleared.
